title: Vanishing of H_1 and of the differentials at a prime gives an etale localization
statement: Let $A\to C$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings making $C$ a finitely presented $A$-algebra, and $\mathfrak q\subset C$ a prime ideal such that the localizations at $\mathfrak q$ of the $C$-modules $H_1(L_{C/A})$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] and $\Omega_{C/A}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] vanish: $H_1(L_{C/A})_{\mathfrak q}=0$ and $(\Omega_{C/A})_{\mathfrak q}=0$. Then there is $h\in C\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $\operatorname{Spec}C_h\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, induced by $A\to C\to C_h$, is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism].

proof.text: *Smooth at $\mathfrak q$.* The $C_{\mathfrak q}$-module $(\Omega_{C/A})_{\mathfrak q}=0$ is finite free (of rank $0$), and $H_1(L_{C/A})_{\mathfrak q}=0$ by hypothesis; $C$ is finitely presented over $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-at-prime-naive-cotangent-criterion] there is $g\in C\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $A\to C_g$ is a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

proof.text: *$A\to C_h$ is an étale ring map.* As $C$-algebras $C_h\cong(C_g)_c$ (both are the localization of $C$ at the multiplicative set generated by $g$ and $c$: inverting $gc$ inverts $g$ and $c$, and conversely). By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-principal-localization] applied to the smooth ring map $A\to C_g$ and $c/1\in C_g$, $A\to C_h$ is smooth [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]: $C_h$ is finitely presented over $A$ and $H_1(L_{C_h/A})=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] (with $B=C_g$, $S=\{c^n\}$), $\Omega_{C_h/A}\cong(\Omega_{C_g/A})_c=0$, since $c$ kills $\Omega_{C_g/A}$ (step 2). Thus $A\to C_h$ is finitely presented with $H_1(L_{C_h/A})=0$ and $\Omega_{C_h/A}=0$, an étale ring map in the sense of Algebra, Definition 00U1 (which Stacks remarks after the definition: a smooth ring map is étale iff $\Omega=0$).

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine] (direction $\Leftarrow$, with $R=A$, $S=C_h$, $\varphi:A\to C\to C_h$), the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}C_h\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] induced by $A\to C\to C_h$ is étale [def-weil-etale-morphism], with $h\in C\setminus\mathfrak q$.
